To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the adenine nucleotide transporter (ANT) does not mediate mitochondrial ATP import in cancer cells, but does in hepatocytes, suggesting that ANT is not essential for ATP import in proliferating cells.
mitochondrial ATP/ADPs are maintained in the presence of respiratory inhibitors by the hydrolysis of ATP generated from glycolysis and are independent of ANT in cancer cells.
the adenine nucleotide carrier (ANT) is required for mitochondrial ATP/ADPs exchange in non-proliferating hepatocytes and other non-cancer cells but not in proliferating cancer cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of mitochondrial function and the role it plays in the Warburg effect in proliferating cells.
the role of ANT in mitochondrial ATP/ADPs in cancer cells.
the role of ANT and glycolytic ATP in mitochondrial function in cancer cells and the role of ANT in cancer cell proliferation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in non-proliferating rat liver hepatocytes, mitochondrial respiration is the major source of ATP and ANT is the primary mechanism for import of ATP into mitochondria.
the ANT is not involved in mitochondrial ATP/ADPMitochondrial ATP/ADP import in proliferating cancer cells.
in cancer cells, glycolytic ATP is imported into mitochondria by an ANT-independent mechanism, and this ATP is hydrolyzed to maintain Δp and ΔΨ.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cancer cell proliferation and glycolysis is not due to a defect in the mitochondrial ATP/ADPi import mechanism.
the Warburg effect is not a consequence of a failure in mitochondrial ATP/ADPsensing, but is a consequence of the suppression of ANT-mediated ATP/ADPexchange.
the ANT isoform expression is regulated during cell cycle progression, which may have a role in the regulation of mitochondrial ATP/ADPratio in the cytoplasm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mitochondrial ATP/ADPs are not dependent on the ANT.
the Warburg effect is not caused by the adenine nucleotide transporters, as previously thought, but by the suppression of the adenine nucleotides transporters.
